name: Generalized claim that real-world headers are/can be UTF-8 encoded vs no such empirical generalization (hedge or ASCII-only stance)
side_a: No deduct when the answer makes no generalization about what real HTTP headers actually carry — i.e., it either states the ASCII-only rule, or merely hedges about trade-offs ('could provide more flexibility', 'depends on requirements') without asserting that headers in practice are UTF-8/non-ASCII encoded.
side_b: Deduct when the answer grounds its recommendation in an empirical generalization that headers are commonly encoded in UTF-8 / commonly carry non-ASCII (e.g., 'more accommodating of common practices where headers might be encoded in UTF-8'), since this asserts non-ASCII header content as the normal case even though it is framed as practice rather than as spec.
